question: Your extraction system pulls findings from quarterly financial filings, industry news articles, and technical specification documents, and a synthesis step combines them into one report for downstream reviewers. The synthesis step currently converts every finding into the same bulleted format. Reviewers complain that revenue figures across quarters are hard to compare and that news context reads as disconnected fragments. How should you change the synthesis output?

options.text: Keep the uniform bulleted format but add a field-level confidence score to each bullet so reviewers can prioritize the most reliable findings.
options.reason: Confidence scores do not fix the format problem. The guide calls for rendering each content type appropriately rather than keeping one uniform format for everything.

options.text: Convert every finding into one large table with fixed columns for claim, value, and source, so reviewers see a single consistent format throughout.
options.reason: This still forces all content into one uniform format, which the guide warns against. News context loses its narrative meaning when it is squeezed into table rows.

options.text: Render the financial data as tables, the news content as prose, and the technical findings as structured lists within the synthesized report.
options.reason: The guide says synthesis outputs should render each content type appropriately: financial data as tables, news as prose, and technical findings as structured lists.

options.text: Rewrite all findings as continuous narrative prose so that the financial figures, news context, and technical details read as one coherent story.
options.reason: This is another uniform format. The guide says financial data belongs in tables, so burying quarterly figures in prose makes them harder to compare.
